title: FlattenOptions.inheritDoc(false) returns declared-only documentation, attributing nothing to a leaf its producer never documented
rationale: This row published a DEFECT until inheritDoc was wired up. It was the repository's signature pathology in the newest code on the branch: the option was declared, defaulted, validated, stored, exposed by a getter and read NOWHERE in src/main, so walkRecord computed the inherited doc unconditionally and inheritDoc(false) was byte-identical to inheritDoc(true). That identity WAS the finding. walkRecord now gates the inherited value at its source, so with the flag off nothing inherited is carried down the walk at all and every leaf reports exactly the documentation its producer wrote about it - which on this schema is none. The emitted docs therefore equal the declared docs, and the probe's two arms now differ, which is what proves the control is live.
catchesBugClass: The control going dead again - a builder method that validates, stores, is exposed by a getter and is never read. The probe expecting DIFFERENT is the tripwire: deleting the conditional in walkRecord turns this row red twice over, once on the verdict and once on the probe. It also catches the over-reach in the other direction, a repair that blanket-nulls documentation rather than only suppressing inheritance: order_id declares its own doc, so this row goes red on its own recording rather than relying on a neighbouring row to notice. That documented leaf was added deliberately - review found the DECLARED_DOC arm satisfied equally by a correct fix and by an erasing one, because every leaf in the schema was undocumented and both implementations produce all-null.
cannotCatch: It cannot show the governance consequence the option exists to avert - ancestor text propagating into a data dictionary as though the producer had written it about that column. That is what enriched-doc-inheritance-attributes-ancestor-doc-to-a-leaf records, and this row is its named remedy. It cannot tell whether the SOURCE of a surviving doc was the field or a coincidence, only that the text matches. And it says nothing about properties, which inheritRecordProperties governs on an independent flag; enriched-record-properties-inherited-by-leaves is that row.

predicted.detail: The consumer asks for declared-only documentation and receives exactly that. order_id declares its own doc and keeps it; the two customer leaves declare none and report none, where inheritance would have attributed 'The buyer' and 'An order record' to them. Both arms of the flag are therefore in one recording, which is the point of the schema change: an implementation that suppressed inheritance by blanket-nulling every doc would satisfy the null half and fail the surviving half. RE-AUTHORED against repaired behaviour rather than overridden - the measurement moved, so this fixture's prediction was rewritten alongside its prose and its id.

probe.note: These two must render DIFFERENTLY for as long as the control is live; the day someone stops reading options.inheritDoc() this flips back to EQUAL and says so.
